label: diffuse token-bigram unit, early steps (s/b/v/n/j after b/i/3/m/d/s)
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps) and combinatorial. It is biased toward early steps: original steps 1-3 (t=2 peaks at 3.1x) and copy steps recall_idx 1-2. It never fires at t=0 or on the delimiter. It prefers the input tokens s, b, v, n, j (s is 6.7x, b 5.1x) and the previous tokens b, i, 3, m, d. The best component found is s at original steps 1-3 after b/i/3/m/d, which has 78% precision but only 10% recall. The best simple predicate (one of s/b/v/n/j right after one of b/i/3/m/d/s, at t<=4) reaches only F1 about 0.35 and mass recall about 0.41 on dev. About 40% of the mass is in the copy phase, at varied positions, and seems to depend on token-pair identities. No single variable has a firing rate above about 7%. The top activations (about 0.24) come from specific bigrams such as b b s, x n, u 2 and e n 2. I did not find a coherent rule for magnitude.
